headline: Tanzid Hasan Tamim scores first Test century on Australian soil
summary: Bangladesh end Day 2 of the first Test in Darwin with a 153-run lead, powered by Tanzid's historic maiden ton.
details: Tanzid Hasan Tamim made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi batter ever to score a Test century on Australian soil, striking 101 off 197 balls in the opening Test in Darwin.
The opener's maiden Test ton included eight fours and a six, marking a significant milestone as he became only the second Bangladeshi to score a hundred against Australia in Test cricket.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto also contributed with a strong 84, while Mushfiqur Rahim added 36 before Bangladesh reached 351 for six at the end of the second day.
Australia's bowling attack, featuring Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, and Pat Cummins, managed to take three quick wickets after tea to slow the momentum.
Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten, sharing an unbroken 43-run partnership to salvage the day's end.
Bangladesh now holds a dominant position with a 153-run lead over Australia's first-innings total of 198 runs at Marrara Stadium.
caption:

Tanzid Hasan Tamim made history by becoming the first Bangladeshi batter ever to score a Test century on Australian soil, striking 101 off 197 balls in the opening Test in Darwin.

The opener's maiden Test ton included eight fours and a six, marking a significant milestone as he became only the second Bangladeshi to score a hundred against Australia in Test cricket.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto also contributed with a strong 84, while Mushfiqur Rahim added 36 before Bangladesh reached 351 for six at the end of the second day.

Australia's bowling attack, featuring Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, and Pat Cummins, managed to take three quick wickets after tea to slow the momentum.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten, sharing an unbroken 43-run partnership to salvage the day's end.

Bangladesh now holds a dominant position with a 153-run lead over Australia's first-innings total of 198 runs at Marrara Stadium.

headline_marked: 8 workers [[killed by toxic gas leak]] at Sitakunda shipyard
headline: 8 workers killed by toxic gas leak at Sitakunda shipyard
summary: The death toll rose to eight after workers were exposed to toxic gas while cutting a cylinder at a ship-breaking yard in Chattogram's Sitakunda.
details: Eight workers have died following a toxic gas leak at a ship-breaking yard in the Bhatiyari area of Sitakunda, Chattogram.
The incident occurred around 9:00 AM on Friday at a factory named Ferdous Steel in the Station Road area of Bhatiyari Union.
Witnesses reported that workers became ill after toxic gas was released while they were using machines to cut a gas cylinder from a scrap ship.
Five workers were initially declared dead upon arrival at the hospital, and three more passed away later.
The deceased have been identified as Sunny Jaldas, Palash Jaldas, Khokon, Rana, Alam, and two brothers, Mansur Ali and Nasir Uddin, among others.
At least two other workers were injured in the incident and are currently receiving treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital.
Authorities are currently investigating the site to determine the exact cause of the gas leak and the subsequent fatalities.
caption:
8 workers dead in Sitakunda. A routine task of cutting a scrap ship's gas cylinder turned fatal.

Eight workers have died following a toxic gas leak at a ship-breaking yard in the Bhatiyari area of Sitakunda, Chattogram.

The incident occurred around 9:00 AM on Friday at a factory named Ferdous Steel in the Station Road area of Bhatiyari Union.

Witnesses reported that workers became ill after toxic gas was released while they were using machines to cut a gas cylinder from a scrap ship.

Five workers were initially declared dead upon arrival at the hospital, and three more passed away later.

The deceased have been identified as Sunny Jaldas, Palash Jaldas, Khokon, Rana, Alam, and two brothers, Mansur Ali and Nasir Uddin, among others.

At least two other workers were injured in the incident and are currently receiving treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital.

Authorities are currently investigating the site to determine the exact cause of the gas leak and the subsequent fatalities.
